messages.subject: loops with ggplot
parts:
sorry to bother again  - I have synthetic data in "all.dat" attached
with conventional plot I get the wanted as this:

ALL <- dget("all.dat")
c10 <- subset(ALL, PCO2 == 10)
with(c10,plot(SID,pH,type="n"))
for (j in 1:length(Alb))  {
for (k in 1:length(P))     {
lines(c10$SID[ c10$Alb==Alb[j]& c10$P==P[k]],
c10$pH[c10$Alb==Alb[j]& c10$P==P[k]]) }}

but I would like to have it in ggplot2 - 

library(ggplot2)

this absolutely doesn't work - 

S <- ggplot(c10, aes(x = SID, y = pH))
for (j in 1:length(Alb))  {
for (k in 1:length(P))     {
S+ print(geom_path(aes(x=c10$SID[ c10$Alb==Alb[j]& c10$P==P[k]],
y=c10$pH[c10$Alb==Alb[j]& c10$P==P[k]])))
}}

How do I do it?

Thanks a lot
Troels

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: loops with ggplot
parts:
Are you by any chance looking for something like this?
xy is the all.dat you sent.

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(xy, aes(x = SID, y = pH, group = Alb)) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(PCO2 ~ P)

Cheers,
Roman

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: loops with ggplot
parts:
Your current approach is way off course.
Make a plot with all the data, and once you're happy with it, subset it within a loop and plot it. Don't call variable names from data.frames a la c10$P. Use only P, and feed `ggplot` function a subsetted (and droplevels-ed) data.frame. You'll probably want to store the result in a list and then maybe use `grid.arrange` from `latticeExtra` to put things together.

Cheers,
Roman
